# The corpus at a glance

*Generated by `terrastat corpus` on 2026-09-11. Recency is measured against 2026-09-09 — the most recent retrieval in the corpus, rather than the date you are reading this, because otherwise a daily series looks stale the moment a crawl ends.*

**Do not edit this file.** Regenerate it after a crawl or after adding a source:

```bash
terrastat corpus --out docs/corpus.md
```

## Length, by frequency

Exact, over every series. The bar is 2 years *of the series' own frequency*, so 2 observations for annual and 24 for monthly; `A3` and `P` step more than a year at a time, so theirs is two observations. `p5 / median / p95` are the 90% extremes of length **within the cohort that clears the bar**.

| frequency | ≥ 2 years | of all | still published | length (obs) p5 / med / p95 | in years | mean obs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| annual `A` | **628.5 M** | 62% of 1.01 B | 550.8 M | 2 / **4** / 24 | 2 / **4** / 24 | 8 |
| monthly `M` | **8.6 M** | 89% of 9.7 M | 7.5 M | 27 / **66** / 294 | 2.2 / **5.5** / 24.5 | 114 |
| quarterly `Q` | **21.8 M** | 78% of 28 M | 16.9 M | 8 / **23** / 109 | 2 / **5.8** / 27.2 | 44 |
| weekly `W` | **250.2 k** | 98% of 254.8 k | 174.3 k | 312 / **809** / 1384 | 6 / **15.6** / 26.6 | 919 |
| daily `D` | **13.4 k** | 96% of 14 k | 12.2 k | 1029 / **5607** / 6676 | 2.8 / **15.4** / 18.3 | 4,633 |
| semiannual `S` | **20.2 k** | 94% of 21.4 k | 12.5 k | 6 / **32** / 68 | 3 / **16** / 34 | 29 |
| 3-yearly `A3` | **517.1 k** | 70% of 735.1 k | 517.1 k | 2 / **3** / 5 | 6 / **9** / 15 | 3 |
| 5-yearly `P` | **842** | 100% of 842 | 842 | 10 / **12** / 12 | 50 / **60** / 60 | 11 |
| biweekly `BW` | **16** | 100% of 16 | 2 | 123 / **905** / 1883 | 4.7 / **34.8** / 72.4 | 757 |
| irregular `I` | n/a | 138.6 k total | n/a | — | — | — |
| unknown `OTHER` | n/a | 2.4 M total | n/a | — | — | — |

`n/a` where a frequency has no fixed period: a length in years and a lag in periods are both undefined for `I` and `OTHER`, so they are counted but not judged.

## What the values look like

**Sampled, not exact** — 267.7 k series drawn across datasets, because this is the only part that has to read the value lists. Series with a single observation are excluded from every column but the first: with one point a series is simultaneously 100% unique and 100% constant.

| frequency | sampled | one point only | distinct values (med) | unique share (med) | constant | near-constant | has a value ≤ 0 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| annual `A` | 88.4 k (250 datasets) | 36% | 9 | 1.00 | 11.8% | 2.4% | 18.1% |
| monthly `M` | 62.6 k (250 datasets) | 3% | 7 | 0.62 | 7.8% | 8.8% | 32.4% |
| quarterly `Q` | 84.1 k (250 datasets) | 9% | 45 | 0.93 | 7.5% | 2.9% | 25.8% |
| weekly `W` | 8.3 k (53 datasets) | 0% | 113 | 0.14 | 4.7% | 30.1% | 32.3% |
| daily `D` | 2.4 k (53 datasets) | 2% | 1,073 | 0.67 | 0.1% | 10.0% | 44.4% |
| semiannual `S` | 4.8 k (22 datasets) | 1% | 26 | 0.98 | 1.3% | 0.2% | 2.0% |
| 3-yearly `A3` | 6.4 k (16 datasets) | 37% | 2 | 1.00 | 6.3% | 0.0% | 2.4% |
| 5-yearly `P` | 564 (3 datasets) | 0% | 11 | 1.00 | 0.0% | 0.0% | 31.2% |
| biweekly `BW` | 16 (4 datasets) | 0% | 592 | 0.99 | 0.0% | 12.5% | 6.2% |
| irregular `I` | 2.4 k (6 datasets) | 83% | 4 | 1.00 | 6.8% | 0.0% | 1.0% |
| unknown `OTHER` | 7.7 k (27 datasets) | 80% | 4 | 1.00 | 4.1% | 0.5% | 31.4% |

`unique share` is distinct values over observations. A long series with a low unique share is a step function or something rounded flat — abundant, and close to worthless as a training example. `has a value ≤ 0` is what decides whether sMAPE, a log transform or a multiplicative model is safe.

## How concentrated it is

Exact. A series count flatters a corpus that is really a few enormous cross-tabulations. `effective datasets` is the perplexity of the series-per-dataset distribution: the number of *equally sized* datasets that would be as diverse as what is actually here.

| frequency | datasets | effective | largest dataset | its share | top 10 share |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|

Read this next to [leakage.md](leakage.md): the more concentrated a frequency, the more a random train/test split puts near-copies of the same table on both sides. `terrastat.dataset.split()` groups by dataset for exactly this reason.
